title: Ukraine disputes Trump's claim of energy ceasefire as Russian diesel deal draws fire
summary: Russian strikes on Ukraine continued a day after President Trump announced an energy ceasefire that neither Kyiv nor Moscow had confirmed. Trump also eased sanctions on Russian diesel, arguing it would bring down US fuel prices, while blaming Ukraine for high energy costs. Andrew Weiss of the Carnegie Endowment explains why the diesel deal barely moves the market and how Washington is using its leverage to push Ukraine toward a deal.
focus: Shadow Andrew Weiss's answers on the diesel deal and on US leverage over Ukraine: he speaks at a steady pace and packs in several idioms per sentence.

vocab.meaning: Act hurriedly and a little chaotically to deal with a problem.
vocab.context: Weiss describes the White House rushing to show action on fuel prices before the midterms.
vocab.example: After the profit warning, the leadership team scrambled to reassure investors.

vocab.meaning: Caught completely by surprise, usually by something unwelcome.
vocab.zh: 措手不及的；被打个措手不及
vocab.context: Ukraine's negotiators had no warning before the diesel decision was announced.
vocab.example: The client felt blindsided when we raised the fee on the final call.

vocab.meaning: Power to influence a person or situation, often because they depend on you.
vocab.context: Refers to the influence Washington holds over Kyiv through weapons and intelligence support.
vocab.example: As their only certified supplier, we have real leverage in the renewal talks.

vocab.meaning: Something you give up or agree to in order to reach a deal.
vocab.context: The fear is that Ukraine will be pressed into broad compromises with Russia.
vocab.example: We can offer a pricing concession if they commit to a three-year term.

vocab.meaning: Reach an agreement after long, difficult discussion.
vocab.context: Used for a deal that would have to be worked out through hard negotiation.
vocab.example: Legal and procurement spent two weeks hammering out the data-sharing terms.

vocab.meaning: Respond to an action by doing something similar in return.
vocab.context: Zelenskyy says Ukraine will stop strikes only if Russia does the same.
vocab.example: If they share their pipeline data, we should reciprocate with our forecast.

vocab.meaning: Done without any reason or trigger from the other side.
vocab.context: Describes how the war was started.
vocab.example: The competitor's price cut looked unprovoked until we saw their inventory levels.

vocab.meaning: The outer edges of a town or city.
vocab.context: Where an energy facility near Kharkiv was hit.
vocab.example: Most of the new logistics hubs are on the outskirts of the city, near the ring road.

vocab.context: Describes buildings damaged in the attacks.
vocab.example: The charred remains of the old plant are still on the site we're assessing.

vocab.meaning: Enjoy and do well in a particular situation, often a difficult one.
vocab.context: Weiss says Trump enjoys springing surprises on allies and rivals.
vocab.example: She thrives on ambiguous problems, so put her on the market-entry case.

vocab.meaning: Unprepared and unsure how to react.
vocab.zh: 失去平衡的；措手不及的
vocab.context: Describes the tactic of keeping counterparts uncertain.
vocab.example: Their surprise bid kept us off-balance for most of the negotiation.

vocab.meaning: Commit even more strongly to a position or strategy, especially when challenged.
vocab.context: European leaders strengthened their support for Ukraine in response to the US move.
vocab.example: Rather than retreat, the board doubled down on the Asia expansion.

vocab.meaning: Arrive suddenly to take action or rescue a situation.
vocab.context: Weiss says Russia can't suddenly come to the rescue of US fuel prices.
vocab.example: A private-equity fund swooped in with a higher offer the day before signing.

phrases.meaning: An amount so small it makes almost no difference.
phrases.context: How Weiss sizes the Russian diesel volume against US demand.
phrases.example: A 2% cost saving is a drop in the bucket next to the margin gap.

phrases.meaning: Achieve visible results, especially early on.
phrases.context: Weiss says the president wants wins he can show voters.
phrases.example: In the first 90 days, the new COO needs to put some points on the board.

phrases.meaning: A lot of fuss about something unimportant.
phrases.zh: 小题大做；茶杯里的风暴
phrases.context: The hoped-for outcome if the diesel row fades quickly.
phrases.example: The press coverage of the reorg turned out to be a tempest in a teapot.

phrases.meaning: Feel relaxed because a worry has gone away.
phrases.context: How observers felt earlier when US support looked secure.
phrases.example: The team breathed a sigh of relief when the regulator approved the merger.
